approaches.name: fiber-optic SCADA/EMS and automated metering for regional grid control
approaches.description: The project deploys fiber-optic communication, SCADA/EMS, automated load-frequency control and metering data systems to enable real-time cross-border grid monitoring, balancing and trading. Practices: Learning-pilot market platform generating transaction data to calibrate algorithms; fiber-optic cables on transmission lines for SCADA/EMS; Fiber optic cable on regional transmission lines; Automated grid stabilization and metering systems; Automated Commercial Metered Data Management System for regional trading; Regional fiber optic network for energy market services; Optical fiber on 220-500 kV lines for real-time grid management; Fiber optic networks along new transmission lines; Advanced metering infrastructure and automated metering data management; Automated load-frequency control and contingency management tools; Automatic Load-Frequency Control for regional grid stability.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: pilot transaction data calibrates market algorithms before scaling - cue: 'learning agenda' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Phase 1 is a deliberate learning pilot that generates the technical, operational, and behavioral evidence to refine market design in Phases 2 and 3.

extra_evidence.text: By standing up a simplified regional platform and core “soft” rules (governance, scheduling, settlement) alongside “hard” enablers (automated metering/MDMS, grid digitalization, fiber communications), Phase 1 produces real transaction, performance, and user‑experience data to calibrate product scope, algorithms, and standards.

These lessons are codified into Phase 2 entry conditions and milestones, guiding the advanced day‑ahead/intraday market design and, subsequently, the fuller market (including regional balancing) in Phase 3—ensuring solutions are Central Asia‑fit before scaling.

These lines will be equipped with fiber optic cables that will facilitate the implementation of a modern Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition/Energy Management System and establishment of an optical communication network.
The proposed project could therefore finance development of a regional fiber optic and digitalization network.

Fiber optic cables can be installed on existing transmission lines. of regional Phase 1 Phase 2–3 interconnections Installation of fiber optic cable • Fiber optic cable connection on the 220kV Shymkent (KZ) – (optical ground wire) on the (i) Tashkent TPP (UZ) cross-border line. construction of 220 kV Kristal (KR) – • Fiber optic cable connection on Uzbekistan-Tajikistan 220-550 kV Yulduz (UZ) cross-border line (ii) interconnections. construction of second circuit 220 kV Uzbekistan-Paulgan-Fergana- Sokin.

Phase 2–3 • Upgrade of telecommunication networks from key power plants to CDC Energia/national dispatch centers. • Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition/Energy Management System upgrade. • Implementation of Automated Grid Stabilization Systems (Automatic Load-Frequency Control and Automatic Reserve & Contingency Handling Mechanism) and advanced metering systems to regulate system frequency, manage reserves, and ensure reliable VRE integration.
Generators’ capabilities on governor control and Automatic Generation Control are critical for regional balancing and frequency regulation.
Component 1 will also support the implementation of an Automated Commercial Metered Data Management System for the United Power System of Central Asia to enhance electricity trading and management.

Developing a regional fiber optic network for energy market services in Central Asia offers significant benefits by improving the monitoring and control of energy infrastructure, enhancing reliability and efficiency.
Pillar 2: Reinforcement, modernization, and digitalization of regional interconnections 12.
The new 500 kV and 220 kV transmissions line to be financed will incorporate optical ground wire and optical fibers will be installed on vital 220-500 kV regional interconnection.
This optical fiber network will facilitate real-time grid management, enable better integration of renewable energy sources and supporting energy trading across borders.
It enables the collection and analysis of large volumes of energy data, informing decision-making processes, and supporting predictive maintenance.

This includes the deployment of advanced metering infrastructure and an automated metering data management system, facilitating accurate monitoring, billing, and data-driven decision-making—critical enablers of regional electricity trading.

Further investments in automated load- frequency control systems and contingency management tools, along with flexible hydropower, will improve real-time grid balancing, reduce reliance on spinning reserves, and support the integration of variable renewable energy sources such as wind and solar.
The phase 3 will also finance the implementation of Automatic Load- Frequency Control to improve frequency stability, optimize economic dispatch, and enhance grid resilience against contingencies.
